messages:
alex: Quick sync — ACME POC needs PrivateLink to our control plane. @marta can you provision interface endpoints in your POC account so we can test Private/VPC deployment?
marta (ACME-SRE): Yep we can. What exact service name, subnets, and SG rules do you need?
josh (InfraEng): I'll DM the exact service name (format: com.amazonaws.vpce.rdinference.prod-<id>) but general reqs: create an Interface endpoint (type=Interface) in 2+ private subnets across AZs, enable Private DNS, attach a security group that allows inbound TCP/443 from the endpoint ENIs (we'll tell you the SG to allow) and allows outbound 443. No public IPs needed.
irina (SolutionsEng): Minimal POC checklist:
  1) Create Interface VPC Endpoint with private-dns-enabled = true
  2) Put it in subnet X and Y (private subnets)
  3) Share the VPC endpoint-id here (we accept on our side)
  4) We'll accept the connection and share a short-lived API key + test hostname
  5) You validate curl to the test URL
josh (InfraEng): AWS CLI example (replace ids):
```
aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint \
  --vpc-id vpc-0abc1234 \
  --vpc-endpoint-type Interface \
  --service-name com.amazonaws.vpce.rdinference.prod-abc123 \
  --subnet-ids subnet-0a1b2c subnet-0d3e4f \
  --security-group-ids sg-0a1b2c \
  --private-dns-enabled
```
marta (ACME-SRE): Do we need to touch route tables / NAT gateway for this? Our infra is locked down.
josh (InfraEng): Interface endpoints create ENIs in your subnets, no route table changes required for the endpoint itself. NATGW only matters for outbound internet egress (e.g., pulling container images). For control-plane PrivateLink traffic you should see traffic stay inside the VPC via the ENIs.
alex: Also check for SCPs or org guardrails that block ec2:CreateVpcEndpoint or ec2:ModifyVpcEndpoint — if those are blocked, we can do an alternative (cross-account peering) but PrivateLink is preferred for security.
irina (SolutionsEng): Test steps after you create the endpoint:
  - post the EndpointId (e.g., vpce-0abc1234)
  - we'll Accept from our account (expect PendingAcceptance)
  - once accepted we'll share test host: https://private-control.redwood-inference.internal/health and a temp API key
  - curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <temp>" https://private-control.redwood-inference.internal/health  -> expect 200
josh (InfraEng): Troubleshooting quick tips:
  - dig +short private-control.redwood-inference.internal  (should resolve to VPC IP like 10.x.x.x)
  - aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters "Name=subnet-id,Values=subnet-..." --query 'NetworkInterfaces[?Description==`Interface endpoint`]' 
  - traceroute to host from a bastion to confirm path
  - if DNS doesn't resolve, confirm Private DNS was enabled on the endpoint
marta (ACME-SRE): One question — for Dedicated pools hosted in our VPC, do those need extra routing to reach the control plane over PrivateLink?
josh (InfraEng): No extra route entries. Your compute nodes will reach the control plane via the endpoint DNS once Private DNS is enabled. If your compute lives in isolated subnets without egress, ensure those subnets can resolve private DNS and reach ENIs. Sometimes internal firewalls block ENI-to-subnet traffic — allow inter-subnet traffic accordingly.
alex: POC cost note: interface endpoints have an hourly cost + data processing. We'll cover up to $50 of POC charges and reimburse anything above with approval.
marta (ACME-SRE): OK creating now in account acct-12345: subnets subnet-0a1b2c, subnet-0d3e4f, SG sg-0f1e2d. Will post vpce id when done.
deploy-bot: NOTE: Endpoint creation detected in acct-12345. Status: PendingAcceptance. We'll notify Redwood infra team to accept.
josh (InfraEng): Received — once you post vpce id I'll Accept from our side and give the test key.
marta (ACME-SRE): Posted: vpce-07f1e2d3c4b5a6. Private DNS enabled.
josh (InfraEng): Accepted from our side. Test host: https://private-control.redwood-inference.internal/health . Temp API key DM'ed to @marta. Run:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <temp-key>" https://private-control.redwood-inference.internal/health
```
marta (ACME-SRE): curl returns 200 and body "OK" from bastion. 👍
irina (SolutionsEng): Great — next steps: we'll stand up a minimal Dedicated pool config and validate model fetch + inference. I'll open a follow-up thread for Dedicated pool sizing.
alex: Thanks team. Closing this loop — if any issues post here and we'll jump on a call.
